clinician.final_diagnosis: Metastatic breast cancer to the gingiva (mandibular gingival metastasis from primary breast mucinous adenocarcinoma)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old female presented to the Clinic for Maxillofacial Surgery with a nonhealing post-extraction wound in the left mandibular gingiva three months after tooth 36 extraction, accompanied by swelling and vegetation of the gingiva. Initial differential diagnosis included pyogenic granuloma, squamous cell carcinoma, and mesenchymal tumors. Gingival biopsy revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma (MAC) with characteristic histology: nests of cells floating in lakes of mucin partitioned by delicate fibrous septa containing capillary blood vessels, with variable cell clusters and occasional tubular arrangements. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated breast origin with ER+ (90%, Allred score 8), PR+ (40%, Allred score 6), HER2 1+, CK7+, CK20+, GATA3+, mammaglobin−, and Ki67 30%. Workup with mammography and breast core biopsy identified a primary breast tumor measuring 60 × 40 × 35 mm in the left breast with infiltrating left axillary lymph nodes. The gingival lesion was confirmed as metastatic breast carcinoma. The patient was referred to the Oncology Committee for Breast Diseases and received 3 cycles of anthracycline (AC) protocol chemotherapy, with subsequent evaluation for radiation therapy to the mandibular metastasis.
